Andrew Moss, CMT@Andy__Moss
02:41 SGTInvesting
It’s about balance and being able to let the trade work.

Pyramiding is great. It’s also harder to do as it has a tendency to magnify discomfort.

If you can take full size, let the trade breathe, and watch it play out till the end, fantastic! Bigger for longer is obviously optimal for trades that are working.

But, if you get antsy when it starts to pullback, thinking about giving back profits, then trimming and trailing is a great method for alleviating that.

Like everything in trading it takes intense discipline. And that’s after you test different methods to find out what suits your mentality best.

Trading around a core is also a good approach. I have no problem adding back to a position if it sets up again with good r/r.

AbCellera’s access to a top tier talent pool in their own backyard is an underappreciated asset that doesn’t show up on the balance sheet.

This passage from Zero to One is over 10 years old, but I believe it is still applicable today.

“Researchers experiment with things that just might work instead of refining definite theories about how the body's systems operate. Biologists say they need to work this way because the underlying biology is hard. According to them, IT startups work because we created computers ourselves and designed them to reliably obey our commands. Biotech is difficult because we didn't design our bodies, and the more we learn about them, the more complex they turn out to be.”

As it pertains to “instead of refining definite theories about how the body’s systems operate”, I am reminded of how the properties of a CD3 binding arm can change depending of the tumor binding arm it’s paired with in a bispecific. Mother Nature is indefinite and you must have the tools to navigate that. Of course, AbCellera seems to have proved they can with their diverse panels of binders and matrices used to define their panels of CD3 binders and optimal pairing: x.com/jackprescottx/…

Now, going after biology that has already been validated in some ways, such as NK3R with ABCL635 is an effective way to not be completely in the dark. Indefinite and definite is a spectrum IMO.

But at the end of the day, doing good science is paramount to success. You need elite minds with good judgement to know what targets are worth pursuing, how the studies should be designed, etc.

“experiment with things that just might work”… You need people with the intuition to know what might just work.

See Booth’s comments in the quoted post below regarding the talent pool AbCellera has access to. Again, this is an under appreciated asset.

$ABCL

(2023) @AbCelleraBio CFO Andrew Booth highlights the strong talent in Vancouver:

“We find ourselves down in the United States at events and conferences and you realize 50% of the room is actually Canadians who have gone down and are living in Boston or in San Francisco. Actually, it's very difficult to start a company in Boston or San Francisco because the war for talent between all of the other companies that are starting to be there. In many ways the talent we have here in Vancouver is a a massive competitive advantage and what we need are great companies that can give them meaningful jobs to allow them to pursue a career in science and engineering.”

BREAKING: Interest expense on US public debt rose +$144 billion YoY in FY2026, or +12%, to a record $1.36 trillion.

This marks the 6th consecutive annual increase, for a total of +$839 billion, or +161%.

For perspective, total receipts rose just +3.2% YoY, to $5.40 trillion.

In other words, interest on federal debt accounted for 25% of total US government receipts.

Meanwhile, Social Security, the largest government expense, jumped +$86 billion YoY, or +5.5%, to a record $1.67 trillion.

At this pace, interest costs will exceed Social Security as the largest government outlay by the end of 2028.

What is the long-term plan here?

He is 19, but he has grown up in the school of Leo Messi: he rests while playing, he works in the areas where he does damage, and he asks to be the leader because he knows that if the ball goes through him, the team will find it easier to win

Tesla VP of Hardware Engineering Lars Moravy explains to Hagerty how the Roadster borrows SpaceX cold gas thrusters to make 0 to 60 possible in 0.55 seconds.

Truly insane:

▫️ 200L carbon-over wrapped pressure vessel
behind seat holds nitrogen at 10,000 PSI
▫️cold gas thrusters push out 80 kN of thrust (equivalent to a single fighter jet engine)
▫️Tesla went with nitrogen because “it just seemed wrong to put fuel into a car” (air is ~80% nitrogen, fair enough)
▫️thrusters same system satellites use to move in space (eg. the “psh psh psh" from Apollo 13 film)
▫️currently takes 6 to 7 hours to refill all nitrogen but Tesla working for it to be 30 minutes
▫️uses leg actuators from Optimus robot to manage downforce on wing

Back in early-September, risk:reward was highly unfavourable if you considered the many macro hurdles I mentioned in my initial post + adverse flow data.

interpretability might be the most important scientific problem in the world right now, as I don't think we can solve alignment if we don't know what we're building. I think I have good news about it. I co-authored early work in mechanistic interpretability at OpenAI and came away pessimistic, because neural networks appeared to fold into arbitrary tangled knots. years later, I started openai's first large-scale automated interpretability project, finding about 2% of neurons legible with the primitive tools we had

with modern agentic tools and a much closer look, the picture looks totally different. the vast majority in models up to trillions of parameters are legible, and their circuits beautiful. many famous examples of tangled neurons turned out to be misunderstood. The roadblocks I expected mostly aren't there. I now think ambitious interpretability will be solved by the time we need it most, and possibly quite soon, as automated scientists keep improving. it may be a bitter lesson for interpretability: the simple thing, at absurd scale, works

21:30 SGTInvesting
Make sure you save this post. This is where the future is heading towards for the stock market.

Here's the top 20 fastest-growing jobs from today until 2035:

1. Nurse practitioners (41%)
2. Solar photovoltaic installers (37%)
3. Data scientists (35%)
4. Wind turbine service technicians (30%)
5. Medical and health services managers (24%)
6. Physical therapist assistants (23%)
7. Psychiatric technicians (22%)
8. Computer and information research scientists (22%)
9. Occupational therapy assistants (21%)
10. Ophthalmic medical technicians (21%)
11. Physician assistants (21%)
12. Information security analysts (21%)
13. Occupational health and safety technicians (19%)
14. Hearing aid specialists (19%)
15. Epidemiologists (19%)
16. Occupational health and safety specialists (18%)
17. Substance abuse, behavioral disorder, and mental health counselors (18%)
18. Home health and personal care aides (18%)
19. Health specialties teachers, postsecondary (18%)
20. Industrial machinery mechanics (18%)

What does this mean for the stock market?

Healthcare:
- healthcare is the largest category on this list. It is literally the future. Huge aging population
- the system also faces a binding capacity constraint. Physician shortages (especially primary care) are projected to persist deep into the 2030s
- home health aides, therapy assistants, and health services managers are scaling to support aging-in-place and higher-acuity outpatient care
- mental health and substance-use roles also reflect a multi-year crisis
- Stocks for advanced practice and managed care: $UNH, $ELV, $HUM, $CI
- Stocks for devices: $ISRG, $SYK, $MDT, $BSX
- Age-related: $LLY, $ABBV, $MRK, $AMGN, $NVO
- Senior housing: $WELL, $VTR

Technology:
- data volume is compounding across every industry (including healthcare records, imaging, and claims)
- data scientists exist to turn that volume into usable signals
- AI requires continuous research, not just implementation.
- computer and information research scientists invent the next algorithms and systems as basic data science becomes more widespread
- connectivity permanently expands the attack surface - Information security analysts grow because the cost of being unsecured keeps rising; especially in healthcare, finance, and critical infrastructure
- stocks for AI infrastructure & platforms: $NVDA, $MSFT, $GOOGL, $AMZN, $AVGO, $AMD, $SNOW, $PLTR
- stocks for cybersecurity: $CRWD, $PANW, $ZS, $FTNT, $S, $OKTA

Renewables:
- solar and wind appear because of the energy transition, but the absolute job numbers remain small compared with healthcare and tech.
- solar photovoltaic installers and wind turbine technicians are high-percentage growth roles tied to new capacity and maintenance.
- these stocks remain more policy-sensitive and cyclical than the healthcare or cybersecurity names.
- stocks for renewables overall: $TSLA
- stocks for solar: $ENPH, $SEDG, $FSLR, $RUN, $NOVA
- stocks for wind / clean energy: $GEV

Industrials:
- industrial machinery mechanics is the main non-service name on the list.
- demand comes from keeping factories, production lines, and equipment running as manufacturing and automation continue.
- this is the more traditional industrial maintenance and equipment side of the economy.
- stocks: $SPCX, $CAT, $DE, $HON, $ETN, $ROK, $EMR

Okay so what to do?
In my opinion, healthcare is the biggest and most durable demand engine on this list. An aging population, doctor shortages, and the move toward more care at home and outside hospitals are already locked in. This is the part of the market that should act as the ballast in a portfolio. Have some real exposure to healthcare.

Tech (data, AI, and cybersecurity) is the higher-upside layer sitting on top of that. These names tend to move more when the market is in growth mode, but they also carry more volatility. So make sure you have exposure here in tech as well for the next decade to outperform the markets.

Renewables and industrial machinery show up on the list, but they are smaller pieces of the overall picture and more sensitive to policy and the economic cycle. It's okay to have crazy volatile names, but make sure you size it correctly.

Whatever happens, let's continue to compound our winners and make millions together.

🚨 Official: Real Madrid statement.

In response to the statements made by Javier Tebas, president of La Liga and vice-president of the Royal Spanish Football Federation, in which he compares the methods of action of the Real Madrid management with those used by Joseph Goebbels, Minister of Propaganda of the N*zi regime, pointing to Real Madrid Television as an instrument of this alleged strategy, Real Madrid CF states the following:

Real Madrid CF considers it absolutely intolerable and extremely serious that someone holding two top positions of responsibility in Spanish football would resort to comparing the club's propaganda methods to those of the N*zi regime in order to discredit it, its management, and its television channel. The clarification that he is not referring to N*zi ideology does not diminish the deeply offensive, morally repugnant, and institutionally undignified nature of his statements.

These statements constitute yet another episode in Javier Tebas's repeated attacks against Real Madrid, its president, and its media outlets. It is unacceptable that he even uses questions, information, or opinions from journalists outside the club to direct his disparaging remarks against us, attributing to us the actions of third parties for which we bear no responsibility whatsoever.

It is particularly serious that Tebas is using these statements to question the legitimate actions of Real Madrid and Real Madrid Television in relation to the Negreira case.

Given the lack of response to the extraordinary gravity of the Negreira case from the two institutions where Javier Tebas holds positions of paramount importance, our club has had to appeal directly to UEFA to demand a full investigation into the payments made for years by FC Barcelona to the Vice President of the Technical Committee of Referees and the adoption of the necessary measures to guarantee the integrity of the competitions.

Real Madrid also demands a complete overhaul of the refereeing system and the federation's governing, management, supervisory, and disciplinary structures, through the replacement of those who held positions of responsibility during that period.

It is particularly significant that Javier Tebas, president of LaLiga and vice-president of the Royal Spanish Football Federation, the organization to which the Technical Committee of Referees belongs, dedicates his efforts to discrediting Real Madrid instead of promoting, from his institutional responsibilities, the clarification of these very serious events and the necessary regeneration of Spanish football.

Javier Tebas's repeated conduct demonstrates a lack of neutrality, respect, and impartiality incompatible with his institutional responsibilities. His constant attacks on Real Madrid and those who demand transparency and reform constitute, in our club's opinion, a true scourge for Spanish football.

For all these reasons, Real Madrid CF believes that Javier Tebas's repeated statements and behavior would be unacceptable in any European sports institution that is governed by principles of respect, neutrality and integrity, and that they disqualify him institutionally from continuing to hold the positions he occupies.
Therefore, Real Madrid CF demands his immediate resignation as president of LaLiga and vice-president of the Royal Spanish Football Federation.

Real Madrid CF will continue to defend its rights, its institutional prestige, the full clarification of the Negreira case and the necessary regeneration of Spanish football.”

The AI revolution is driving an unprecedented export surge across Asia:

South Korea’s exports jumped +83.5% YoY in September, the largest annual increase on record and the strongest increase among the major Asian economies.

Furthermore, Singapore’s exports soared +46.2% YoY in August, while Malaysia and Taiwan recorded gains of +45.5% and +41.0% over the same period, respectively.

This was followed by Vietnam’s exports rising +39.1% YoY in September, while China’s exports increased +25.0% YoY in August.

Japan recorded the smallest gains, but its exports still advanced +19.3% YoY in August.

The surge was driven by strong AI-related demand, particularly for semiconductors, electronics, computers, and other technology products.

South Korea’s semiconductor shipments alone jumped +263% YoY in September.

AI demand is fueling a historic surge in Asian exports.

Personal dip buys from today: $AVGO, $MRVL, $KLAC

$AVGO:
- Feels like the market has overlooked Broadcom YTD.
- I think they're still one of the best positioned in the networking theme thanks to exposure to many diverse areas - optical DSP, Tomahawk, Jericho.
- Future growth should accelerate via Tomahawk 6/7 ramping in 2027, Tomahawk Ultra, optical DSPs.
- Obviously there are risks with Broadcom but I ultimately see earnings upside = stock should re-rate (at some point lol).

$MRVL:
- Investor day last week basically confirmed that they're a scaleable AI infra name...not just custom silicon / DSP.
- Feels like Marvell's opportunity is now much bigger than most people thought.
- E.g. other than 800G/1.6T....NPO/CPO, and scale-out + up.
- Still think it's early from them with many areas yet to ramp volumes e.g. 1.6T and NPO/CPO.

Overall, feels like both Broadcom and Marvell are very well positioned. Broadcom keep adding XPU customers + extend those deals with hyperscalers. Marvell keep growing, very high torque right now IMO.

$KLAC:
- Down 42% in 3.5 months and haven't had a position before and wanted to take one lol - more so as a re-rating trade rather than a longer-term hold.
- No real in depth thesis, more so a risk/reward play in the broader "AI quality" ecosystem I'm tracking.
- Especially when compared against other semicaps like $LRCX / $AMAT that are well ahead in YTD %.

Obviously these aren't your sexy names like $NBIS, $INTC or $BE - but I feel like I built my positions in these types of names earlier in the year (was a little late to the Intel party) and don't want my core portfolio to get overly concentrated.

That said, I'm well aware that semis earnings are right around the corner and that many of these bottleneck type names have de-rated.

But as of right now, I'm sitting slightly on the cautious side by not attempting to time bottoms here.

Recent flow data has been tragic for semis, so would rather wait to see a few days of +ve net flows first to get some confidence that investor fatique isn't a permanent scar. There's only so much tolerance investors have for multiple >20% drawdowns in a matter of months.

Paradis@ParadisLabs
02:40 SGTInvesting
On the AI trade, it feels like the market is digesting two issues at once:
1. Financing costs
2. Hardware bottlenecks

One reason that AI stocks are down is that the market did not like OAI's ARR number from last week. That reaction continued today after Anthropic's ARR number came out yesterday.

Whether that's the rational market reaction is up for debate, but fundamentally, it's crucial to remember that the AI trade rests on the abilities of the AI labs to justify their spending commitments by growing their top/bottom lines at a healthy rate.

I think it's clear now that the market has some jitters surrounding AI lab ARR's, with the market most probably testing whether their spending commitments are justifiable.

Since total token consumption continues to rise, I highly doubt this market sell-off is driven by demand-side factors.

However, with AI hardware names selling-off significantly...it seems like the market has some jitters around the supply-side. Current bottlenecks (e.g. power, memory, networking) ultimately restrict data centers from being powered up quicker and in turn, restrict the end-beneficiaries (the hyperscalers and frontier labs) from growing numbers at a rate the market can stomach.

Bottlenecked segments like memory or networking still do have various risks such as price wars, China, capex effects and investor positioning. But to me, it feels like the dip gets bought on Q3 earnings particularly with low investor positioning factored into the equation. Whether they can be sustained winners long-term is up for debate.

**It's also vital to remember that the market still has various other hurdles to contend with also -- Iran, oil, yields, midterms and Anthropic's IPO all impacting short-term positioning.
